markdown.markdown:
Instructor – University of Washington
Course: ECON 200 Introduction to Microeconomics
Terms: Autumn 2021
Selected Student Comments:
“This was my first econ class, but I thought the topics were incredibly interesting. I found myself applying so many of the concepts that we learned to other thinks in my daily life. Overall it really made me think and I enjoyed it.”
"What contributed most to my learning was asking clarification questions to the Professor because they really helped me clear my doubts."
"I appreciated how Frida was wiling to re-explain a concept that someone didn't get and really took the time to make sure our questions were getting answered. Examples she drew on the chalkboard during class time were very thorough and useful."
Instructor – University of Washington
Course: ECON 300 Intermediate Microeconomics
Term: Winter 2022, Spring 2022, Summer 2022, Winter 2023, Spring 2023
Selected Student Comments:
“Good preparation of the class agenda and content. It was intellectually engaging and concepts were presented quickly and clearly enough to keep my interest.”
"I loved this class, although it is technical the real world applications stretched my thinking."
"I saw how this class is a building block for the rest of econ. It helped me to understand the "why" of the question."
Instructor – University of Washington
Course: ECON 301 Intermediate Macroeconomics
Terms: Autumn 2022
Selected Student Comments:
“It made me think of economics in a very different way than before.” "There were many new concepts and a relatively more rigorous approach to creating models, which was interesting."
"I really enjoyed learning Economics with Frida. I appreciate how approachable and willing she was to help me. I will definitely keep an eye out if she is ever teaching a 400-level course! "
